questions.prompt: What is the inverse of the relation `R = {(0, 3), (5, 1)}`?
questions.explanation: The inverse swaps each pair: `(0, 3)` becomes `(3, 0)` and `(5, 1)` becomes `(1, 5)`.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: A scalar has size only. Distance is a scalar; force, acceleration, and displacement all have direction, so they are vectors.

questions.prompt: What is `i³`?
What is `cot x` equal to?
questions.explanation: Cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent: `cot x = 1/tan x = cos x/sin x`.

questions.prompt: What is the mode of the data set `4, 7, 7, 10, 10, 10, 12`?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often; `10` appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.prompt: If `f(x) = 3x - 2` and `g(x) = x + 6`, what is `(g ∘ f)(4)`?
What is the inverse of `f(x) = 7x + 14`?
questions.explanation: Swap to get `x = 7y + 14`, so `7y = x - 14`, giving `y = (x - 14)/7`.

questions.prompt: For which values of `x` is `(x + 1)/(x² - 9)` undefined?
questions.explanation: Set the denominator to zero: `x² - 9 = 0` gives `x² = 9`, so `x = 3` or `x = -3`.
Multiply every term by `2x`: `6 + x = 4`, so `x = -2` (which does not make the denominator zero).

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the line through `(-3, 2)` and `(1, 10)`?

questions.explanation: Subtract real parts (`7 - 3 = 4`) and imaginary parts (`-2i - 5i = -7i`): `4 - 7i`.

questions.prompt: What is the dot product of `(-4, 3)` and `(2, 6)`?
If `tan x = 2/9`, what is `cot x`?
What is the negation of the statement "Some students passed the exam"?
questions.explanation: The negation of "some do" is "none do". So "Some students passed" is negated by "No student passed".

questions.prompt: A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 to 8. What is `P(landing on a multiple of 3)`?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3 from 1 to 8 are `3` and `6` (two of them), so `P = 2/8 = 1/4`.

questions.prompt: Which of these functions is NOT one-to-one over all real numbers?
questions.explanation: `(x - 3)²` gives the same output for inputs equidistant from 3 (e.g. `2` and `4` both give `1`), so it is not one-to-one.

questions.prompt: If `f(x) = x² + 1` and `g(x) = 2x - 3`, what is `(g ∘ f)(x)`?
questions.explanation: Apply `f` first, then `g`: `g(f(x)) = 2(x² + 1) - 3 = 2x² + 2 - 3 = 2x² - 1`.

questions.prompt: What is the vertical asymptote of `f(x) = (x + 4)/(2x - 6)`?
questions.explanation: Set the denominator to zero: `2x - 6 = 0`, so `x = 3`.

questions.prompt: What is the horizontal asymptote of `f(x) = (5x + 2)/(x² - 1)`?
questions.explanation: The bottom degree (2) is larger than the top degree (1), so the horizontal asymptote is `y = 0`.

questions.prompt: Which equation represents a parabola?
questions.explanation: A parabola has exactly one squared variable. `x = 2y² + 5` squares only `y`, so it is a parabola; the others are an ellipse, a hyperbola, and a circle.

questions.prompt: What is the determinant of `[[-2, 5], [3, -4]]`?
What is the inverse of `[[4, 2], [3, 2]]`?
Simplify `(5 + 5i)/(1 + 2i)`.
questions.explanation: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate `1 - 2i`: top `= (5 + 5i)(1 - 2i) = 15 - 5i`; bottom `= 1 + 4 = 5`; so `(15 - 5i)/5 = 3 - i`.

questions.prompt: For what value of `k` are the vectors `(3, k)` and `(6, -4)` perpendicular?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular means dot product is 0: `(3)(6) + (k)(-4) = 18 - 4k = 0`, so `k = 18/4 = 9/2`.

questions.prompt: What is the magnitude of the vector `(-7, 24)`?
The range of a data set is 40 and its largest value is 52. What is the smallest value?
questions.explanation: Range `= largest − smallest`, so `40 = 52 − smallest`, giving smallest `= 52 − 40 = 12`.

questions.prompt: What is `i¹⁵`?
questions.explanation: `i¹⁵ = i¹² · i³ = 1 · (-i) = -i`, since `i¹² = (i⁴)³ = 1` and `i³ = -i`.

questions.prompt: If `p` is true and `q` is false, what is `¬(p ∨ q)`?
questions.explanation: `p ∨ q` is true (since `p` is true), and the negation of true is false.

questions.prompt: What is the inverse of `f(x) = 2x³`?
questions.explanation: Swap to get `x = 2y³`, so `y³ = x/2`, giving `y = ∛(x/2)`.

questions.prompt: Using Cramer's rule for `3x - 2y = 1` and `x + y = 7`, what is `y`?
questions.explanation: `D = (3)(1) - (-2)(1) = 5`. `Dᵧ` replaces the y-column with the constants: `Dᵧ = (3)(7) - (1)(1) = 20`. So `y = Dᵧ/D = 20/5 = 4`.

questions.prompt: Solve `x/(x - 2) = 3`.
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by `(x - 2)`: `x = 3(x - 2) = 3x - 6`, so `-2x = -6`, giving `x = 3` (which is valid).

questions.topic: Equation of a line through two points
questions.prompt: What is the equation of the line through `(2, 1)` and `(5, 7)`?
If `p` is true and `q` is false, what is `(p ⇒ q) ∨ (¬q)`?
questions.explanation: `p ⇒ q` is false (true ⇒ false), but `¬q` is true (since `q` is false), so `false ∨ true` is true.

questions.prompt: From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of a tower 50 m away is 30°. How tall is the tower? (`tan 30° ≈ 0.577`)
questions.explanation: `tan 30° = height/50`, so `height = 50 × 0.577 ≈ 28.9 m`.
